ratings.comment: Great professor, kind, understanding & really cares about his students . The quizzes, mid term and final are not hard. DON'T cheat because he is good at catching copied work. He also puts hidden prompts or hidden text in assignments to catch students who use AI. If you pay attention, study, and do the work yourself, you should do well in his class.

Just don't cheat. Assignments contain ghost prompts that will be implemented into your code if you decide to use AI, and he uses that as a grounds of emailing you and demanding an explanation. Don't copy someone's code either. Also don't tab out of quizzes. Other than that, very understanding and chill professor who cares about his students

DO NOT CHEAT. he is sneaky and hides hidden prompts within text if you're using AI. He doesnt use lockdown so do not be tempted to switch tabs. He cares about students and is understanding to everyone. He gives quizzes and programming projects. THe programming can be difficult and you have to self teach yourself. Use online resources but dont cheat

Great guy, but beware of sharing programming assignments; he will catch on and give you no credit for that assignment. He reuses quizzes, midterms, and finals from previous semesters with slight variation (90% the same) so ask someone from previous section for answers for an easy A. Aside from that, he is actually a cool person.

Not a lot of assignments besides programming projects, which you have to do alone, and he is very strict about cheating/use of AI on quizzes and projects. However, students are given a lot of time to complete the projects. Exams are like the quizzes, and he allowed a cheat sheet, but you have to ask for it to be provided for the midterm and final.

Best prof in cpsc I've had! He makes c++ so easy to understand and also fun! Highly recommend taking him! He is also the nicest, and caring prof on campus in my opinion bc I had to miss for a bit and he was lenient about me missing quizzes + midterm. If you put in the work, you will succeed. You don't need to cheat to pass his class. Take him!

Really nice professor who tells a lot of jokes and makes class enjoyable. Be aware that attendance checks started this semester—some students say they didn't happen before. Quizzes are simple if you study a little. Overall, I highly recommend this class!

Better than Terrell. All quizzes and exams are taken on Canvas. Responds to emails quickly if you have any questions. Exams are similar to the quizzes! Plenty of extra credit given throughout the semester!

An amazing and very experienced professor. He made me remember why I liked learning CS. The difficulty of the class is about what you should expect from a CS class at this level so put in the effort you think you need. Don't cheat since he is VERY attentive to it. Overall, one of the best CS professors in the entire department. Highly recommended!

His lectures are like having a conversation with a professor. He's pretty chill but takes cheating very seriously. No AI and if you tab out on the quizzes he will send you to his office. Quizzes every other week plus a couple of EC assignments and for attendance. Material posted doesn't really help so being in class will give you info you need.

Solid professor, learned a lot. I highly recommend using a second device when taking his quizzes, he won't hesitate to summon you to office hours if he catches you switching tabs. Him and his TA's actively check the canvas log files to catch cheaters on his canvas quizzes.

6 quizzes,6 PAs,2 Exams and he also gives extra credit at the end. BE VERY CAREFUL when attempting to cheat on canvas quizzes. I highly recommend you use a second device like a laptop or phone to find answers. He takes cheating very seriously as in he will summon you to office hours to plead your case. A lot of us got -1 on quizzes for tabbing out.

The only homework was a few programming projects that can be finished in a few hours. The programming assignments cover a wild variety of things. One of them focused on maxheap and all are different programming language, some very old languages. He can go on tangents that help us more than material, but quizzes seem to be from the textbook.

Great professor, Attend his lecture and make sure take note. 6 assignment and 6 quiz, 1 midterm and final. So make sure do all exam and attend the quiz. His grading is base on point, each exam 100 point, so assignment and quiz matters. He also curve and give a extra credit at the end.

Chill dude, I enjoyed learning C++ from him. Remember a few important things though. Don't tab out on quizzes or exams you will get a -1 and go to the dean. If your code matches on PAs there is a decent chance he will give you a -1. He gave us 5% extra credit.

Solid professor. Provides you all the resources you need and is engaging in his lectures. Very understanding and laidback so don't hesitate to ask him anything because he is willing to listen and answer. Make sure to study because he may not go over some content fully. You do have to show up for quizzes and exams, but going to lectures is optional.

Very fun professor, has 6 coding hw and 6 quizzes. While C++ might be hard at the beginning he is very helpful and open to questions. Midterm and final are based on quizzes so make sure to study those carefully and take your time analyzing each question for tricks.

Learning C++ and Linux might be intimidating to some but luckily Professor Gold teaches it in a way that is fun and makes sense, including giving some real life examples that he has had or real life events that relates to what is being taught. The quizzes can be little tricky so be sure to read the code carefully. And yes, C++ is the best language.

Professor was funny, engaging, interactive, and helpful. Most of his content is during lectures with little powerpoint and other additional links so it's kind of important to show up. Heavy C++ with some difficult projects if not started early. Tests and Quizzes are based on lecture

Great Lectures! They are not off slides, so it sometimes is hard to review so show up to class and take notes. Try to learn the basics of c++ before you start. He says its ok if you don't know in the beginning, but he doesn't really teach the syntax so it's easy to get confused the first few weeks. Exams are heavily based off quizzes!

Graded by PA's, Quizzes, and Exams. PA's are manageable if you get help from TA, tutor, friends. He doesn't post much notes to study for quizzes, so study outside resources, a lot of it, to ace. He's a good prof & lecturer, but isn't always prepared. Must use vim for code and questions on quizzes, but you can code on vscode and output with wsl.

Steve is one of the professors in the CS department who truly stands out. Amazing lectures, great feedback, and programming assignments that allow you to digest the course's content fully. Quizzes were pretty tough as the expectation is for you to dig deeper into the concepts but they prepare you well for the exams!

I recommend learning the basics of C++ before taking this course. Coding assignments and quizzes are based on previous assignments, so make sure you understand how your programs work behind the scenes. No lecture slides, Gold just shows up and starts teaching. Classes felt more like a conversation rather than a lecture, which was cool.
Cool professor but lectures are freestyle which make material hard to understand. Quiz and test are not bad.

Lectures really aren't useful if you already understand C++. There isn't much Linux after the first month either. His quizzes don't really align with the lectures sometimes and the programming assignments can be done quite easily. However, he will dock your grade for any minor mistakes made on those assignments. Super cool guy who cares though.
Definitely a great professor who enjoys teaching his teach very much.

Don't confuse professor Gold for Goldstein. They are the OPPOSITE! Professor Gold's lectures were very informative and helped immensely on each coding project he had provided. Quizzes and exams were a bit difficult for me which is why I got a B, but not once did I study and got the majority of the info from his lectures alone.

Funny guy, chill, and laidback. Class is graded based on 6 projects, 6 quizzes, 2 exams, and a lab section. Projects aren't too difficult, but the last 2 require more time. Quizzes and exams weren't too bad either. Lab is group work. Lectures were actually pretty entertaining, concise, and informative. Overall, great professor, easy A/B

Professor Gold is an amazing and caring guy. He explains concepts so well and is so funny. Apart from some tough quizzes, his projects are nothing too hard and exams aren't bad either. Do well enough and he might even let you skip the final. If you are ever confused don't hesitate to ask questions, he will help!

Professor Gold is very approachable and gives great lectures to follow. His grading criteria sometimes isnt the clearest, but his teachings and enthusiasm makes up for it completely. Highly recommend him for anyone wanting to learn and enjoy in doing so.

His projects are very clear, he explains everything well, and his lectures are engaging. I felt like I was actually learning C++ and having fun. Other CS professors I've had at this school feel like they're actively trying to prevent you from learning but that is not the case here. I would recommend.

He's really good at posting recorded lectures. He's a really nice guy who genuinely wants his students to do good in his class. I really enjoyed his class. I'm taking him again for C++. You'll be totally fine if you do all your assignments on time. His demos for projects are just screenshots of your code output.
Pretty good lecturer and tries his best to answer students' questions. Easy class if you just do your projects on time. Quizzes and exam are really easy too.

Only take Gold for 277 if you're willing to put in the work to learn. He does a good job teaching during the lectures, but for the actual assignments, you are pretty much on your own. If you put in the work needed, you will learn a ton. For the 6 quizzes and 2 tests, there was nothing on them you wouldn't learn just from doing the work assigned.

This was my first c++ class and was fairly easy. Gold is a really good professor and he actually cares about what he's teaching as well as his students. The homework assignments aren't too hard and he pretty much teaches you everything you need to know for them in class. Midterms/Quizzes are mostly easy.
If you don't take Gold for 274 you're actually making the biggest mistake of your life.

Great guy and great professor; quiz after every program, 1 midterm 1 final, study for exams using previous quizzes as your guide bc the questions will likely be the quizzes, can opt out on final if satisfied w/ current grade, in class participation is encouraged. Choose this professor, you'll thank me later.

This class is not that bad until you hit BigInts. BigInts will be the hardest project in the class. Stsrt early. Also, do not take this class with PHYS 152 at the same time. Second, C++ is a lot harder than expected. You may have to review C++ again for 326, 328, 424. If you follow lectures, and projects, then midterm and final should be ok.
Overall a good professor. The only problem is he does not give notes in the class and his lectures are all based on the lab assignments which he gives.

He crakes jokes 24/7 and encourages students to learn C++ to be the main language! Quizzes are based on the projects, so make sure you do THEM! Blizzard and gaming companies heavily rely on C++! Don't freak out because Master Gold is willing to guide you to understand the concepts at anytime! Can't wait to join the programming team next fall!

Well, this class atm is pretty cool rn. He crakes jokes 24/7 and references real life situations to have students really learn C++ the best way as possible. The most challenging part of C++ is the projects. The quizzes are based on the projects, so make sure you do THEM! C++ is main program of industries! Can't wait to join the programming team!!!!
His quizzes and exams are very difficult and different from the lecture! First two projects were easy but after that, they became harder and harder!

I didn't like his class because i didn't learn much. Took him for 282 thinking he's a good prof based on reviews but it turned out way different. I wouldn't take him again ever. His grading criteria isn't really clear.

He is extremely passionate about what he teaches. Imagine taking a class from a goofy dad in programming with 10/10 teaching skills. The lectures are a blast because of the stories he tells which tie into the lesson. I finished the midterm and final in less than 20 minutes.

Gold is a golden professor. C++ can be tricky, but Gold makes learning the language as easy as possible. No homework, but you'll almost always be working on a project that helps you learn the material. The last project, Memory Manager, is the shortest but also the hardest project that takes the most time. You may/may not have optional final.

His notes help a lot with the projects up until the last two projects. His tests were similar to the projects and quizzes. Some of the quizzes were way different from his projects. You have to demo your project to him in person before you can turn it in for credit. You can tell he really likes programming. He was available for questions during lab.

1st day class,did class activity, sat in 1st name order, talk about ur new friend in front of class.420 total pts,294pass. 6 projects and 5 quizzes 20 pts each. 1 mid and 1 final both 100 pts each. know project 2 and 3 op overload and cout friend operator for midterm. final had 2 op overlo like mid, sort, map like quiz5, and mem manager like quiz6.

He's cool. This class was just a repeat of a Java class except you learn the C++ syntax and some cool things about C++. If you're good at programming in any other language then this class is just an easy A.   Just don't hard code. People did that and he will catch you.

Professor Gold is an absolute beast, he rides a motorcycle. I call him Professor Thahab. Lectures are very important to survive the class, but it's not mandatory. His quizzes and tests correspond with the study material took in class and lectures. He explains a lot on projects during the lectures. What an absolute beast!

I love professor gold! I've had him for 274 and 282 now. Make sure you attend lecture! Although it isn't mandatory, he does go over how to do the projects and other important concepts very well. Exams are based on quizzes. One project  and quiz (on the current project) every 2 weeks. Super easy to talk to!

I loved professor Gold. His quizzes and tests were directly related to the material he taught in class. Pay attention in class, and try to participate - you will learn more. The only qualm  I have is that I wish he taught more and at a faster pace; I wish he challenged his students a bit more. Overall, great class. I recommend this class!

Wonderful professor! Important to go to lectures, he explains projects and quizzes during that time. I love him because when he teaches there's no doubt he actually enjoys the material. You can clearly tell CS is his passion, not just his work. Final optional. Quizzes and Midterm are easy (if you attend lectures). My favorite professor in CS!
Great teacher, lectures are interesting and funny. The projects can look tough at first but he give clear explanations to do them. Quiz are really easy and are the main part of the midterms.

Professor Gold is am amazing professor! His lectures are very  interesting but his bi-weekly projects can be a bit complicated.. He does go over the projects in class though and he is always willing to help.

Prof. Gold was great. His quizzes were sometimes tough but I passed all of them with A or B grades. The cool thing was if you were happy with your grade you could skip the final and he would give you the grade you had.

Gold is a great professor and his lectures are really helpful in understanding the concepts. Programs range from easy to very confusing but he is very helpful in explaining things in lecture if you have questions and gives a lot of time to complete. Quizzes for every program, 1 midterm (easy), 1 final ( easy,review midterm concepts).
He is a good professor. The projects are challenging, but the quizzes are pretty easy. The midterms are same of all the quizzes.

Took him for an upper division graphics programming class. He didn't know the language we used, only a similar language. We spent every lecture watching hour long lecture video tutorials of a guy talking over powerpoint. I wasted my upper div elective with this class, I wish he put more effort into it.

Professor Gold is one of my all-time favorite teachers at CSULB. He is inspirational, funny and engaging. You will want to be part of the class and will enjoy every moment. He is extremely knowledgable about computer programming and has had years of experience. Fantastic teacher!!!

Gold is the most chill professor in the department. Not stuck up or strict, like some teachers can be. If you're interested in the material, you can learn a lot from Gold, because he's always willing to help. Assignments aren't too rigorous, but challenging enough to learn something.

Steve Gold is a great teacher! His lectures are fun: he is very easy going and good at explaining the concepts. Programs are somewhat challenging, but definitely doable. Tests are very easy if you finished the lab assignments. Take him!

Awesome guy, very funny. Projects are reasonable and some fun even fun. He may surprise you with a gift before the final exam. ( "I LOVE YOU STEVE GOLD" ) If you are looking to have an easy ride, gold is the man. From what I hear, if you want a very in depth understanding and a challenge, go for neal terrel.

Steve does a fine job in this course. His labs were a little tough, but after searching for examples online and reading the book they were doable. Some of the labs build upon each other so it helps to get it right the first time. He was really generous in showing us an example of a previous exam so it helped in preparing for the midterm.

Mr. Gold is very laid back as far as lectures go. He has HW assignments due every week based on the reading of the textbook. Some of the assignments really help in putting your final project together. Quizzes were the same problems as on the midterm so be comfortable with them. One semester-long project so the workload isn't alot for the most part.

Class is super easy, I failed because I chose to not turn in any of the homework, which is apparently worth as much as a test.  So, turn in all of the homework and then you can basically half-ass everything else to get a good grade.  He doesn't curve and don't expect him to help you out if you're on the verge of a better grade.
Easily the best Comp Sci teacher I've had. In fact, it's thanks to him I chose Comp Sci over Engr. Coaches the programming team as well. Be careful though, his assignments can get quite long.

he's one of the BEST!! the way he teaches and how he puts his program assignments together is AWESOME! quizzes n tests are pretty easy. haha laid back fun guy. RECOMMENDED! =D i had a great time haha would gladly take him again for any other class. you're gonna end up with a buncha games when you're done with his class LOL! (his programs are games)
TOok it a while back but really enjoyed class...He was very clear and helpfull..I always felt like i knew what I was doing..

Generally something of a slacker but not a bad professor just the same. The consensus is that Pompei is the better professor in terms of getting the lessons across but I found Gold's lessons to be understandable and effective.  Labs were at times a bit demanding but nothing unreasonable.
Gold is the nicest teacher i had out here. Actually he's not, but that's cos he's as nice as pompei and konig, but easier! definately recommeneded
Good at explaining.  Not too many assignments.
take his class.  he is super.  easy to learn and explains throughly.
